title: Closed models [notes postérieures à PS ?] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continuing pp. 13 and 15). A is a small category and B = Δ. (A×B)^ is the category of presheaves on A×B, i.e. simplicial objects in the presheaf topos A^. Simplicial sets M ∈ B^ act on it through p_A^*(M) = e_{A^}⊠M, giving the cotensor (power) X^M := Hom(p_A^*M, X) (internal Hom in (A×B)^). Here B's simplicial sets are pulled back to A×B, and the degree-0 part is taken by restricting along the B-direction (written (-)_0, via p_{B*}).

Line 1. (X^{Δ_n})_0 = X_n. This is Yoneda in the simplicial variable: the n-th object of a simplicial object is the 'Δ_n-power evaluated in degree 0'.

Line 2. (X^{∂Δ_n})_0 = Hom(∂Δ_n, X) = lim←(X_{n-1} ⇉ X_{n-2}). This is the matching object M_n X, i.e. the limit of the face diagram. The page also notes it equals (Cosk_{n-1}X)_n. The sketched triangle, its boundary labelled by 1-simplices, illustrates ∂Δ_2.

Lines 3–4. For a map X → Y of simplicial presheaves, Grothendieck writes the pullback-power map X^{Δ_n} → X^{∂Δ_n} ×_{Y^{∂Δ_n}} Y^{Δ_n}. Its degree-0 component is the relative matching map X_n → M_nX ×_{M_nY} Y_n. Requiring these maps to be fibrations (in A^ or some model structure on it) is precisely the Reedy fibration condition. So he is setting up the Reedy-type (or SM7-type) structure on simplicial objects in A^ via cotensors.

Right-hand computations. A_n = A records that a constant simplicial object A has all A_n = A, with X_{n-2} ≡ X_{n-1} denoting the face maps. He then asks ('??') what Hom(∂Δ_n, a) and Hom(M, a) ⇉ a are for a constant object a = p_B^*a. By adjunction, Hom(X×M, a) ≃ Hom(X, a^M). Testing on generators α⊠β gives Hom(α⊠(β×M), a⊠e_B) ≃ Hom(α⊠β, a⊠e_B). Page 15 draws the conclusion L^M = L for L ∈ A^, M ∈ B^, meaning constant objects are 'discrete' for the simplicial cotensor. The bottom ('Hom', 'L') is abandoned.

Purpose. These are preparations for model structures on simplicial objects / bisimplicial-type presheaves, with matching objects and the fibration condition, in the Pursuing-Stacks-era 'closed models' study.

Verso. The reverse is recycled IBM JCL for compiling and link-editing MODULEF (the INRIA finite-element Fortran library). It is not mathematics.
errors: The claim (page 15, prepared here) that L^M = L for every M ∈ B^ is false in general. Correctly, Hom(α⊠γ, p_A^*L) = Hom(p_{A!}(α⊠γ), L) = Hom(α,L)^{π0(γ)}, so (p_A^*L)^M = p_A^*(L^{π0(M)}). It equals L only for connected nonempty M, e.g. Δ_n and ∂Δ_n with n≥2. For ∂Δ_1 one gets L×L; for ∂Δ_0 = ∅ one gets the final object.
Correspondingly, the identification Hom(α⊠(β×M), a⊠e_B) ≃ Hom(α⊠β, a⊠e_B) needs π0(β×M) = π0(M) = point, i.e. M connected.

This traces back to the 'Proposition' on p.13 asserting Hom(L'⊠M', L⊠M) = Hom(L',L)×Hom(M',M) for all presheaves. The correct formula is Hom(L',L)^{π0 M'} × Hom(M',M)^{π0 L'}. The extension-by-colimits argument fails because (L',M') ↦ L'⊠M' does not preserve colimits in the pair, e.g. coproducts. It is valid for representables or connected objects.
The notation lim←(X_{n-1}, X_{n-2}) is shorthand for the matching limit over the face diagram of ∂Δ_n. This is fine for n≥1, but it degenerates for n=0,1 (M_0 X = final object, M_1 X = X_0×X_0).

deep.surprise_reason: Routine set-up of matching objects and Reedy-type fibration conditions for simplicial presheaves, all standard since Reedy and Bousfield–Kan. The only notable feature is a small error: the connectedness hypothesis is forgotten in L^M = L and in the p.13 full-faithfulness claim.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: the 'Hom_{B?}' before p_{B*} is struck out. Read: (X^{Δ_n})_0 = p_{B*}(Hom(p_A^*(Δ_n), X)) = X_n.
Line 2: 'lim' carries a left arrow underneath, i.e. lim← (projective limit) of the face diagram X_{n-1} ⇉ X_{n-2}.
'(Cosk_{n-1} X)_n' is followed by a struck-out symbol. It is the gloss for (X^{∂Δ_n})_0.
The triangle sketch has its edges/vertices labelled by small 'Y_1'/'x_1'-type symbols (1-simplices on the boundary). It illustrates ∂Δ_2 ⊂ Δ_2.
'X_{n-2} ≡ X_{n-1}' is a multiple-arrow diagram (face maps) between X_{n-1} and X_{n-2}, not an identity.
The final line reads approximately Hom(α⊠(β×M), a⊠e_B) ≃ Hom(α⊠β, a⊠e_B), cut off at the right margin.
The rotated typescript is MODULEF JCL (//ETAP1 EXEC PGM=FLIPFLOP ...), with handwritten edits such as '13040' and 'IEBUPDTE'. It is unrelated to the mathematics.
